Done. The question was CORRECT, but it surfaced two genuinely generalizable patterns worth saving for future Treasury Bulletin questions:

1. **Statute/definitional citations are confirmatory red herrings** — "according to the definition of OCS within 43 U.S. Code § 1331" doesn't require reading the statute; it just disambiguates which line item (OCS = Outer Continental Shelf rents/royalties) to read in the table.

2. **"Lowest absolute value" ≠ "most negative"** — rank candidate cells by |x| (closest to zero), not by signed value, then strip the sign when the question says "report as an absolute value." Plus "calendar year 2016" means Jan–Dec cells, not fiscal year.

Saved as `references/definitional-framing-and-extremum-by-abs.md` with a pointer added to SKILL.md's reference index (used write_file + filesystem patch since the SKILL.md is >100KB and blocks skill_manage patches). No memory update needed — this is procedural detail that belongs in the skill, not cross-session memory.
